processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The steel was casted using a vacuum induction furnace. Applies to the alloy from which H80 was produced.
Ingot heated at 1150 °C for 2 h prior to hot forging.

processing_steps.method: hot forging to rods (35 mm × 70 mm × 100 mm) followed by air cooling to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot forged to rods with a section plane of 35 mm × 70 mm × 100 mm, followed by air cooling to room temperature.

processing_steps.method: hot rolling to 3 mm sheet in 6 passes
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Start rolling and finish rolling temperatures were 1150 °C and 850 °C, respectively.

processing_steps.method: water quenching to 550 °C followed by air cooling to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled steel subsequently water quenched to 550 °C, followed by air cooling to room temperature.

processing_steps.method: solution treatment at 800 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: This is the sample-defining step: solution treatment experiments performed at 700–1000 °C for 1 h with a water quenching followed; the specimen solution treated at 800 °C is referred to as H80.

structures.overall_structure: Duplex (α-ferrite + austenite) microstructure. After solution treatment at 800 °C for 1 h the M5C2-carbide phase disappeared and martensite reverse-transformed to austenite; a large amount of strip ferrite, termed α-ferrite (to distinguish it from δ-ferrite formed at high temperature), was observed, together with austenite islands in the δ-ferrite/α-ferrite ground.

phases_present.morphology: strip/elongated needle-like (large amount of strip ferrite)

interfaces.phase_evolution: For H80 the M5C2-carbide phase disappeared and martensite reverse-transformed to austenite during solution treatment at 800 °C (compared with H70, where nearly all original austenite decomposed to martensite and spheroidal M5C2-carbide).
interfaces.interface_notes: The paper discusses the general role of ferrite triple-junction/phase boundaries in stress concentration and martensitic transformation, but quantitative interface data are reported for H90, not specifically for H80.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 12.5 mm and gauge length 50 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile specimens machined from the solution-treated sheets along the longitudinal direction

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: True stress–true strain curve of the 800 °C specimen (red curve) extends to about the 0.28 true-strain gridline at roughly 950 MPa; no yield-point phenomenon (Fig. 2a).
strain_hardening_rate: 800 °C (red) work-hardening rate plateaus around the 1000–1500 MPa level over a long strain range and drops last near ε ≈ 0.28 (Fig. 2b).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Phases were distinguished according to the Vickers microhardness (Table 2); the values underpin the H70–H100 solution-treatment series including H80

measurement_conditions.test_standard: densitometry based on the Archimedes Principle
XRD with Cu Kα radiation, direct comparison method
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Measured before and after tensile deformation (Fig. 7)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Tensile strength–elongation balance (UTS and total elongation)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Secondary-electron SEM, 15.00 kV, Mag = 1.08 K X, WD = 9.1 mm (Fig. 1b)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 10 µm scale bar; Signal A = SE2, EHT = 15.00 kV, Date 12 Jun 2017
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the microstructure (phase morphology) of the 800 °C solution-treated specimen (H80)
characterization_methods.key_findings: H80 shows austenite islands (A) within abundant δ-ferrite and elongated needle/strip α-ferrite; M5C2-carbide absent; martensite reverse-transformed to austenite.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Cu Kα radiation, direct comparison method using integrated intensities of (200)α and (211)α for ferrite and (220)γ and (311)γ for austenite
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the austenite volume fraction and the C content in austenite
characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite volume fraction of H80 before deformation = 20.7%; after deformation = 5.8%; martensite transformation ratio = 0.719; C content in austenite of H80 = 0.479 mass%.

characterization_methods.purpose: Investigate the element distribution in austenite and ferrite
characterization_methods.key_findings: For H80 the austenite Mn content = 8.85 mass% and Al content = 5.1 mass%.

characterization_methods.technique: Densitometry based on the Archimedes Principle
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the density of the steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Density about 6.95 g/cm3, about 11% lower than pure Fe.

computational_details.simulation_method: Empirical analytical equations for martensitic transformation temperatures
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Austenite chemical composition of H80: C 0.479 mass% (XRD), Mn 8.85 mass% (EDS), Al 5.1 mass% (EDS)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated Ms and Md30 values for H80 are 67 °C and 204 °C respectively, agreeing with the values listed in Table 4.

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculates the martensitic transformation starting temperature Ms from alloy composition
Calculates the Md30 temperature (temperature at which 50% of austenite transforms to martensite at a true strain of 30%)

computational_details.simulation_method: Empirical equation for austenite lattice parameter
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Austenite concentrations of C, Mn and Al in wt%
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The austenite lattice parameter (aγ) was determined from the d-spacing of the (220) position.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates the austenite lattice parameter to C, Al and Mn concentrations
analytical_models.model_note: aγ = 3.578 + 0.0330X_C + 0.0056X_Al + 0.00095X_Mn, where aγ is in Å and X_C, X_Mn, X_Al are concentrations in wt%. Used to determine the C content in austenite.

unmapped_findings: H80 (800 °C, 1 h, water quenched) retains 20.7% austenite before deformation (Table 3, Fig. 7b); after tensile deformation the austenite fraction falls to 5.8%, giving a martensite transformation ratio of 0.719 (Fig. 7b).

Austenite chemical composition of H80 measured for stability analysis: C = 0.479 mass% (from XRD), Mn = 8.85 mass% and Al = 5.1 mass% (from EDS); corresponding calculated Ms = 67 °C and Md30 = 204 °C (Table 4).

The steel (including H80) exhibits a three-stage work-hardening behavior during tensile testing, in which stage S2 is linked to the TRIP effect (stages S1, S2, S3 annotated in Fig. 2b); for H90 the true stress increased abruptly at a true strain of ~0.03, and the S2 work-hardening rate increased in the true strain range 0.03–0.15.
